# C01 — catalogue baseline B

I found four useful references through permitted catalogues and verified each against an opened primary source. This is an internal-model translation of those references into the supplied problem, not evidence that the proposed combination was deployed or proved effective.

1. **controller-runtime v0.6.3 shared-informer cache and keyed reconciliation** — https://pkg.go.dev/sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime@v0.6.3/pkg/cache

   Its shared-informer cache and deduplicated reconciliation queues provide a concrete way to replace repeated API polling with change-driven processing of recurring schedule objects and their Jobs. The cache documentation exposes informer event handlers, cache synchronization and field indexing; the package overview describes queued, deduplicated reconciliation. Adaptation would watch the relevant resources and reconcile their current state. Wait for cache synchronization and preserve a time-based wake-up for future schedule occurrences: a clock advancing does not itself change a Kubernetes object. Dependency compatibility and last-success status logic remain implementation responsibilities.

   Discovery catalogue: https://github.com/pperzyna/awesome-operator-frameworks
   Date evidence: the opened v0.6.3 documentation and version index date this version to September 15, 2020, before the October 2, 2020 cutoff.

2. **robfig/cron v3 parser and scheduling semantics** — https://github.com/robfig/cron/blob/master/README.md

   Its standard cron parsing, timezone behavior and overlapping-run wrappers offer reusable schedule semantics and edge-case references while Kubernetes remains responsible for Job creation. The dated upgrade notes describe minute-first parsing by default, optional seconds, timezone changes and wrappers that delay or skip overlapping callbacks. Preserve the existing controller API's schedule interpretation when using these ideas. The wrappers operate on local callbacks; they do not establish cross-process Kubernetes Job concurrency, missed-run behavior or persistent success status.

   Discovery catalogue: https://github.com/uhub/awesome-go
   Date evidence: the primary README explicitly dates the relevant v3 upgrade section to June 2019. This supports that section's availability, not the age of every current README statement.

3. **Prometheus Go client v1.7.1 instrumentation** — https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/prometheus/client_golang@v1.7.1/prometheus

   Its counters, histograms, timers and HTTP metric exposition can measure controller throughput, reconciliation duration and the delay between a scheduled occurrence and Job creation. I would keep processing time separate from scheduling delay so queue congestion and slow reconciliation are distinguishable. Define units, buckets and bounded label dimensions, and expose the metrics from the controller. These measurements do not replace a persistent API status field.

   Discovery catalogue: https://github.com/uhub/awesome-go
   Date evidence: the opened v1.7.1 page and version index both show June 23, 2020. The also-opened v1.25.0 page is dated October 8, 2026 and is retained separately as later evidence; it was not backdated. The old release is historical evidence of the mechanism, not a recommendation to deploy that exact version.

4. **Enterprise Integration Patterns: Idempotent Receiver** — https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/IdempotentReceiver.html

   Duplicate-safe processing can keep repeated notifications, resyncs or retries from creating extra Jobs for the same scheduled occurrence. The pattern supplies two approaches: deduplicate repeated input or make repeated processing have the same effect. A controller-specific translation would give each intended occurrence a stable identity and reconcile creation attempts against the API. The pattern does not define Kubernetes transaction boundaries, conflict handling or recovery after a successful create followed by a failed status update.

   Discovery catalogue: https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/toc.html
   Date evidence: the opened catalogue revision history, https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/history.html, records adding the pattern in March 2003. This dates the named mechanism, not every word on the live definition page.

**Combined application and remaining gap.** These references support an informer/cache observation path, keyed reconciliation, preserved cron semantics, duplicate-safe creation and explicit throughput/latency instrumentation. My translation is to update the latest-success status while reconciling successful owned Jobs and to retain that value when old Job objects are cleaned up. I did not locate a verified reference specifying that exact status field or its persistence contract within this run. Its treatment of missing timestamps, competing completions and status-write conflicts therefore remains a design decision.

There were 25 open/click attempts, including repeated reads of the same URL, covering 20 distinct opened URLs; ten additional find calls inspected already-opened documents and are logged separately. No open attempt failed. One search snippet from the excluded kubernetes/community tree was returned by the search engine, recorded as an exposure and not opened; it did not identify a recognized target proposal. No gold, other run, repository history or target proposal document was read. General model pretraining knowledge cannot be erased.
